decisions.question: Who signs off on go-live?
decisions.prefillValue: Jeff Kelly (named in sage.json as go-live decision maker candidate, transcript-referenced) and/or Roger Greenhagel (President, Peerless — formal authority identified via vera.json web research). Confirm routing path with Ashley.

decisions.question: Which ComputerEase company codes are in scope?
decisions.prefillValue: Company code 00 confirmed for IL/WI Home Depot residential (from transcript Ashley Salerno demo 2026-04-16). Additional codes for IN and OH operations may exist.
decisions.rationale: Only company code 00 was explicitly mentioned in transcripts. Peerless operates in IL, IN, OH, and WI — additional company codes for Indiana/Ohio operations are possible. Client must confirm complete list.

decisions.question: Expected transaction volume — leads per day, jobs per week, documents per week
decisions.prefillValue: Inferred from company size (~$15M-$32M ARV, 7-branch regional contractor): 10–30 HD leads/week standard, 40–80 during spring/summer peak (March–September). 5–15 'Save as Final' jobs/week. 5–20 contract documents/week.
decisions.source: Inferred from vera.json company.revenueBracket + industry patterns for residential fence contractor
decisions.rationale: No explicit volume figures in transcripts. Estimates derived from company size, revenue bracket, and residential contractor industry norms. Client must confirm actuals.

decisions.question: CI/CD tools in use
decisions.prefillValue: None — inferred from first-engagement posture (no CI/CD mentioned in any scoping call). Brian Cook is the IT director but stated he is not the integration owner.
decisions.source: Logical derivation from project.json (isNewToDataSkate: true) + transcript signals
decisions.rationale: CI/CD tools were never mentioned in 4 scoping calls. Brian Cook's comment 'I'm in to GCP only to debug, not to operate' implies no pipeline tooling. DataSkate will configure from scratch.

decisions.question: Logging and monitoring tools
decisions.prefillValue: Anypoint Monitoring (DataSkate standard for all MuleSoft IaaS engagements). No client-side monitoring platform mentioned.
decisions.source: DataSkate standard default (pipeline/PLANNING_CONTEXT.md) + no client monitoring tool mentioned in transcripts
decisions.rationale: DataSkate standard applies. Client has not named any monitoring platform. Brian Cook manages GCP but no application-level APM was discussed.

decisions.question: Failure notification recipients and channel
decisions.prefillValue: Ashley Salerno (ashley@peerlessfence.com) — primary operational contact for all 4 flows. DataSkate on-call (raghuram@dataskate.ai) always notified. Notification channel: email (Slack not confirmed in use at Peerless).
decisions.source: vera.json buyerMap.people[] + transcript evidence (Ashley owns all manual processes)
decisions.rationale: Ashley is the operational owner of UC1–UC4. No alternative operational contact identified. Slack not mentioned — email is safest default until confirmed.

decisions.question: Post go-live support ownership
decisions.prefillValue: DataSkate (IaaS model — recommended). Peerless has no in-house MuleSoft developer. Brian Cook confirmed he is not the integration operator.
decisions.rationale: IaaS is the recommended model explicitly. The rationale includes 'Peerless has no in-house MuleSoft developer; Brian Cook has explicitly stated he is not the integration owner.'

decisions.question: Data residency requirements
decisions.prefillValue: US only — inferred from Peerless's footprint (IL, IN, OH, WI). CloudHub 2.0 US East-1 region recommended for Midwest clients.
decisions.source: Inferred from vera.json company.hqLocation (St. Charles, IL) + DataSkate standard for US-only clients
decisions.rationale: No international operations indicated. Standard US-only stance applies. US East-1 is the DataSkate standard for US Midwest clients.

decisions.question: Uptime SLA
decisions.prefillValue: 99.5% (DataSkate IaaS standard for mid-market construction vertical). Equivalent to ~43 hours downtime/year.
decisions.rationale: No SLA specified in transcripts. 99.5% is appropriate for a midmarket construction contractor where downtime during business hours is disruptive but not catastrophic.

decisions.question: Peak load times / seasonal patterns
decisions.prefillValue: Spring/summer peak (March–September) — residential fence installation is highly seasonal. March–May: permit/approval backlog clears. May–August: highest install volume. Pattern inferred from residential construction industry norms.
decisions.source: Inferred from vera.json company.industry ('residential fence installation') + industry patterns
decisions.rationale: Residential fence installation in the Midwest peaks with warm weather. Ashley's mention of a 'lot of ideas on the business process' (Raghuram 2026-04-14) suggests volume pressure exists. Actual peak dates must be confirmed.
